subject: Delegated derivatives / escrow workflow and proof of non-training
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@medinovahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@medinovahealth.com>, procurement@medinovahealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: escrow for derivative works and proof of non-training

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the call last week. Legal has one remaining ask before procurement can move our PO forward: we need a short, reproducible workflow that shows how Redwood prevents customer interaction data from being used for model improvement, and how derivative outputs (e.g., generated text) are governed if we want escrow/escrow-like custody for outputs.

Specifically: 1) what artifacts do you provide as "proof" that requests were not included in training datasets; 2) if we request an escrow arrangement for generated deliverables, what format/transfer options exist; 3) list of subprocessors involved in any transfer path.

Can you provide something we can attach to the DPA amendment? We prefer an itemized checklist or short playbook.

Best,
Asha 
Asha Patel
Head of Procurement, Medinova Health
asha.patel@medinovahealth.com


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@medinovahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@medinovahealth.com>, procurement@medinovahealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: escrow for derivative works and proof of non-training

Hi Asha —

Absolutely — attaching a short evidence playbook and our current subprocessor inventory. Quick summary inline below to keep things actionable for legal/procurement: 

1) Proof of non-training (artifact set)
   - Operational artifact: ingestion logs & KV-cache-isolation report (timestamped)
   - Policy artifact: model-serving config showing "training: disabled" flag per tenant
   - Audit artifact: reproducible trace (request id -> serving host) and daily retention snapshot for the request window

2) Escrow/derivative custody options
   - Option A: SFTP export of deliverables (PGP or TLS) with custody metadata + retention SLA
   - Option B: Transfer to customer's on-prem S3 with signed manifest and hash list
   - Option C: Escrow via 3rd-party custodian (we can generate signed manifests on upload)

3) Subprocessors
   - See attached CSV: includes host regions, purpose, and whether they have access to persistent storage of request payloads.

I'll loop in David and Kim internally to confirm operational feasibility and add the minimal attestation language your legal team prefers. If this looks directionally right, I can provide a one-page workflow diagram and a short attestation paragraph to append to the DPA.

Thanks — talk soon.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Product Compliance | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-evidence-playbook-v1.pdf (summary playbook)
Attachment: subprocessor-inventory-2026-05.csv

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify: escrow for derivative works and proof of non-training

Team — forwarding Asha's note and the attachments (playbook + subprocessor CSV). Procurement wants a concise, auditable workflow and a one-paragraph attestation we can paste into the DPA amendment. Questions: 

- David: can the serving runtime produce the ingestion logs + "training: disabled" per-tenant config extract on demand for a given timeframe? How long to produce per-request traces?
- Kim: can Legal/Trust consume a CSV of subprocessor access and our standard retention snapshot? Any red flags if customer requests SFTP export to a EU-based endpoint?
- Jonas: if they ask for escrow with a third-party custodian, what cryptographic signing options do we have for manifests and who owns keys?

I propose we keep the attestation narrow: we attest that (a) requests from Medinova for the specified tenant were processed with model improvement disabled; (b) we provide the listed operational artifacts within the stated SLA; (c) derivatives can be exported under the listed options. No new contractual commitments beyond DPA amendment unless legal advises otherwise.

Please reply with short bullet answers so I can share with Asha by EOD tomorrow.

Evelyn

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify: escrow for derivative works and proof of non-training

Evelyn / team — quick answers: 

- Ingestion logs & per-request traces: yes, runtime stores per-request metadata (request id, model variant, serving host, timestamp). For a single request trace we can produce a signed bundle within 24 hours; for bulk windows (e.g., a week) we usually need 48-72 hours depending on timeframe.

- "training: disabled" config: we persist tenant flags in our deployment registry. We can export a cryptographically signed snapshot of the tenant config that shows model_improvement=false for the requested interval. 24 hour turnaround.

- Subprocessor CSV: Kim, the CSV identifies subprocessors with storage access. If customer requests EU SFTP export we need to confirm region routing and if KMS restrictions apply — that is a standard ops note, not a blocker.

- Escrow signing / keys: Jonas — can you confirm what we can sign with customer-supplied keys vs our HSM? We support signed manifests with our HSM; sharing customer-managed keys requires a separate key exchange and likely more legal control.

I'll draft a short operational attestation paragraph for Evelyn to review.

-David

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify: escrow for derivative works and proof of non-training

Short answers from infra/security: 

- We can produce signed manifests using our HSM (RS256) for any export. That includes PGP-like hash lists and signed JSON manifests.
- Customer-managed keys: we can support wrapping a transfer with a customer-provided public key so they can verify signatures locally; we cannot hold customer private keys in our HSM without an additional KMS agreement.
- If they want a third-party escrow custodian to hold derivatives, we can transfer via TLS to the custodian and generate signed manifests at time of upload. We recommend the custodian have an API we can push to (S3-compatible) so we can automate manifests and TTLs.

Ok to give Asha a one-paragraph attestation + the playbook and CSV. Suggest the attestation language: 

"Redwood attests that for the Medinova tenant configured under Tenant ID <redacted>, model-improvement was disabled for the timeframe specified, and Redwood can produce ingestion logs, a signed tenant config snapshot indicating model_improvement=false, and signed export manifests for derivative deliverables within the stated SLA. Exports can be routed to customer SFTP, customer on-prem S3, or an approved third-party escrow custodian; cryptographic manifests are produced using Redwood's HSM and can be verified by recipients. Any requirement to use customer-managed private keys or to hold keys on behalf of the customer will require a separate KMS arrangement."

If that reads fine to Kim/Legal, we can share with Asha and copy the playbook link.

Jonas
